az_papago_park.blurb: Papago Park is a city park in central Phoenix, just north of Tempe, with scattered buttes of brown conglomerate. Most of that rock is soft and crumbly, so only a few spots are worth a rope. Hobo House, a small breakaway butte on the southeast side, has firmer stone and the most developed bolted lines. The 15 climbs here are nearly all sport, mostly easy to moderate at roughly 5.5 to 5.8, with a pair of harder lines at 5.10 and 5.11, plus one trad route and an easy boulder problem. Think of it as a quick urban outing rather than a destination crag, and inspect old hardware before trusting it.

az_end_pinnacle.blurb: End Pinnacle is the granite spire that caps the Rockfellow Group's northwestern tip, out in the East Stronghold of southeastern Arizona's Cochise Stronghold. The climbing is mostly multi-pitch trad, usually two to six pitches, with a few bolted lines mixed in. Grades cluster between 5.10 and 5.11, with a couple of 5.12 pitches. Expect a full day: the walk in gains about a thousand feet, the lines are exposed, and the way down is a string of rappels with scrambling between them, so a second rope is wise. It rewards confident trad leaders who want long, committing routes.

az_teenage_mutant_ninja_turtle_crag.blurb: This crag sits low on the Catalina Highway on Mount Lemmon near Tucson, at a hairpin turn with a roadside pullout. The cliff faces north along a very narrow canyon, only a few feet across, where jammed boulders and trapped sand form flat ledges for belaying. Of the 15 routes, ten are bolted sport, four are trad and one is a top rope. Grades run from about 5.5 to 5.10, with the biggest cluster at 5.9, and the bolts are painted to blend into the stone. It suits newer leaders and cool-season days at low elevation, though rock on this part of the mountain can be variable.

az_amateur_hour_crag.blurb: Amateur Hour Crag is a northwest-facing cliff of pale rock with grey bands on lower Mount Lemmon above Tucson, at around 4,700 feet. It stays in shade for most of the day, which helps in warm weather. Ten of its 15 routes are sport and five are trad, spread from about 5.6 to 5.11 with plenty in the 5.8 and 5.10 range, so a mixed party can find something suitable. Getting there takes roughly 20 minutes on the Ruins trail followed by an off-trail traverse over terraces, and the final approach can be awkward when water is running high in the drainage.

az_draw_pile_the.blurb: The Draw Pile is one of seven sections of Crags Against Humanity, a set of roadside cliffs low on Mount Lemmon's Catalina Highway near Tucson. Its main wall faces northeast and can be seen from the road. Of the 15 routes, 14 are bolted sport and one is trad, graded from about 5.7 to 5.10, with most at 5.9 and below. That, plus generous bolt spacing and chunky holds, makes it friendly for beginners and intermediate leaders. Shade arrives by mid-morning, so warm days are tolerable, but this is a busy spot with highway traffic and shooting noise nearby.
